What the tiers and flags mean
STRONG
A BET with cover probability of 56% or more and no flag that blocks STRONG.
BET
Cover probability of 53% or more and positive EV at DraftKings' line, with no SKIP flag.
SKIP
A BET my rules say not to bet as is: a new-QB SKIP or a REVIEW flag. Tap "Why SKIP?".
No bet
DraftKings has a line but the model's side doesn't clear the BET bar (its side is shown in gray).
No line
DraftKings hasn't posted this game yet; the model's line is shown.
Why SKIP?
New-QB SKIP: a starting quarterback isn't in the ratings (the opening QB is gone, or the new starter hasn't started this season). REVIEW: your manual entries would move the line by more than 1.5 points.
Why not STRONG?
On a BET at 56%+ that a rule kept from STRONG: the reliability flag (the edge leans on one less reliable part of the model), an interim head coach on the team picked, or a bowl game.
Notes
Information only, never changes a pick: QB change in the last 3 games, status unverified after a bye, possible injuries, an opponent's interim coach, or a reliability flag on a pick under 56%.
Top factors
The three biggest pieces of the model's line (offense vs defense matchups and home field).

The tiers and dropdowns are a display of the workbook's BET, STRONG and flag columns; nothing here changes a pick.

Covering / Not covering / Push tags compare the live score with the DraftKings line logged for the pick. They're unofficial until Sunday's grading.

What the tiers and flags mean
STRONG
A BET with cover probability of 56% or more and no flag that blocks STRONG.
BET
Cover probability of 53% or more and positive EV at DraftKings' line, with no SKIP flag.
SKIP
A BET my rules say not to bet as is: a new-QB SKIP or a REVIEW flag. Tap "Why SKIP?".
No bet
DraftKings has a line but the model's side doesn't clear the BET bar (its side is shown in gray).
No line
DraftKings hasn't posted this game yet; the model's line is shown.
Why SKIP?
New-QB SKIP: a starting quarterback isn't in the ratings (the opening QB is gone, or the new starter hasn't started this season). REVIEW: your manual entries would move the line by more than 1.5 points.
Why not STRONG?
On a BET at 56%+ that a rule kept from STRONG: the reliability flag (the edge leans on one less reliable part of the model), an interim head coach on the team picked, or a bowl game.
Notes
Information only, never changes a pick: QB change in the last 3 games, status unverified after a bye, possible injuries, an opponent's interim coach, or a reliability flag on a pick under 56%.
Top factors
The three biggest pieces of the model's line (offense vs defense matchups and home field).

The tiers and dropdowns are a display of the workbook's BET, STRONG and flag columns; nothing here changes a pick.

Every upcoming FBS game by kickoff (33 games).

What the tiers and flags mean
STRONG
A BET with cover probability of 56% or more and no flag that blocks STRONG.
BET
Cover probability of 53% or more and positive EV at DraftKings' line, with no SKIP flag.
SKIP
A BET my rules say not to bet as is: a new-QB SKIP or a REVIEW flag. Tap "Why SKIP?".
No bet
DraftKings has a line but the model's side doesn't clear the BET bar (its side is shown in gray).
No line
DraftKings hasn't posted this game yet; the model's line is shown.
Why SKIP?
New-QB SKIP: a starting quarterback isn't in the ratings (the opening QB is gone, or the new starter hasn't started this season). REVIEW: your manual entries would move the line by more than 1.5 points.
Why not STRONG?
On a BET at 56%+ that a rule kept from STRONG: the reliability flag (the edge leans on one less reliable part of the model), an interim head coach on the team picked, or a bowl game.
Notes
Information only, never changes a pick: QB change in the last 3 games, status unverified after a bye, possible injuries, an opponent's interim coach, or a reliability flag on a pick under 56%.
Top factors
The three biggest pieces of the model's line (offense vs defense matchups and home field).

The tiers and dropdowns are a display of the workbook's BET, STRONG and flag columns; nothing here changes a pick.

From the season sim (10,000 rest-of-seasons from week 10). 2026-27 rule (collegefootballplayoff.com): the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC champions and the highest-ranked Group of Six team (no title required) get in, plus the next 7 highest-ranked teams; seeded straight 1-12, top 4 get byes, no reseeding. "Ranking" here is the sim's committee stand-in: rating minus 5 pts per projected loss. Rough, not the committee.

Coach Power Rankings

Current FBS head coaches. Score = weighted z-scores: Level vs talent 36%, 4th-down decisions 18%, Second-half adjustments 14%, Results vs expectation 14%, NFL draft development 10%, Player development 9%. Each component is a career average over rated seasons (2016-26, 2020 out; 2026 by games so far; results vs expectation and development from 2019), shrunk toward average, so coaches with few seasons sit near 0. Value over talent = pts/game vs the preseason prior; development = EPA/game above recruiting expectation; 4th downs = pts/game vs the best expected-value call; second half = EPA/play ×100, opponent-adjusted; results = wins per 12 games vs the model; NFL draft = draft position above what the 247 star level predicts, per season (players with 2+ seasons under the coach, credited by share of their college seasons; draftees credited shown). Display only: none of it feeds the picks.

Service academies (Air Force, Army, Navy): 247 talent doesn't measure academy rosters, so their value over talent is measured against what academy programs typically do (last season's rating and returning production plus an academy adjustment); their results vs expectation are measured against the academy average too (the model's pregame odds share the talent problem: academies beat them by 1.5 wins per 12 games), and NFL draft development doesn't apply (N/A; their score uses the other components). 4th downs: option offenses face more short 4th downs, which would cost them points if they punted; their credit comes from going for it (the expected-value call), and their higher conversion rate (academies 75% vs 63% expected) isn't credited. Top-talent teams beat the talent-based prior more than the rest (top 10%: +2.7 pts/game); not adjusted, so it stays in those coaches' value over talent. Level vs talent view: how good a coach's teams were vs teams with the same 247 roster talent (final rating vs a talent curve fit on all FBS teams; academies vs the average academy), with no last-season term, so keeping a team above its talent counts every year. It is the main score and rank (since Nov 6): it takes value over talent's place with the same weights; the value-over-talent score and rank are shown as the alternate view.
